newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SCA says might delay planned fine paper price lift.
newsitem.headline: SCA says might delay planned fine paper price lift.

text.p: Swedish forestry group SCA said on Thursday it may have to delay this spring's planned fine paper price rise but said it should be able to lift liner and coated paper (LWC) price in the second quarter.
"On the fine paper side we will probably have to postpone the planned price hike," SCA's chief executive Sverker Martin-Lof told Reuters.
"I hope pulp prices can rise around mid-year. This would help fine paper prices."
But regarding liner, which is raw material for corrugated board, and LWC (Light Weight Coated) paper he was more optimistic.
"We have a strong order book on the liner side," he said.
"It is completely full...and we hope to be able to raise prices gradually during the second quarter. Also on LWC we expect to be able to gradually raise prices in the second quarter."
Martin-Lof did not see any signs that general forestry trends would turn for the better any earlier than this autumn, when he hoped to see a change.
"Many have said the turnaround would come earlier, but we haven't thought so," he said. "There is no clear trend showing this that I can see."
The forestry sector has been struggling with high inventory levels, low demand and price pressure on their products since the autumn of 1995 when pulp prices plunged from $1,000 a tonne.
But this week, several forestry groups in North America, Finland and Sweden have announced possible price hikes on pulp as of May 1 to $580 a tonne from the current level of $520.
